messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: region=us-west-3 primary GPU pool at 98% utilization, request queue growing. autoscale attempts failing (quotaExceeded). Observed 4.1k queued requests, 95th latency > 12s on generation APIs. Potential broad customer impact. Pager: @oncall-anna @sre-maya :rotating_light:

oncall-anna: @incidents-bot got the page, investigating. Can we get the exact autoscaler error logs and the route table state?

sre-maya: grabbing logs now. early sign: autoscaler is hitting cloud quota on provisioning new GPUs - requests being rejected with 403-like errors. Queue growth started ~7m ago.

eng-runtime-lead: what's the policy for cross-region steering? we have standby pools in us-east-2 and eu-west-1. We can start steering non-low-latency traffic to east2 but need to ensure KV cache fallbacks are ok.

palmer: tagging customer-impact list. From metrics, 3 customers have >30% error-rate increase: acme-inc (prod), beta-saas (staging->prod overlap), and internal smoke runs. Support notified.

support-jordan: I've posted in #support-escalations and pinged acme contact. They report timed-out chat responses.

eng-runtime-lead: autoscaler error snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:43Z autoscaler.go:214 provision request failed: quotaExceeded: requested 4 gpus, available quota 0 for project redwood-prod-uswest3
stack: cloud-provider/compute.Provision
```

infra-ops: Confirmed - we're at a regional quota limit for that SKU (A100-like). Cloud ticket open but ETA for quota raise is 2-4 hours unless we move capacity.

oncall-anna: options: 1) manual emergency scale via reserved global pool (we have small hot spare in dedicated-reserve), 2) reroute low-priority and best-effort traffic to us-east-2, 3) enable circuit-breaker to reject new best-effort requests and protect SLA customers. Which sequence?

sre-maya: prefer steer+breaker to avoid manual infra changes. initiating traffic steering for non-SLA routes now. I'll also flip circuit-breaker to reject "inference.low-priority" route.

eng-runtime-lead: be careful: steering implies fallback model variants (quantized) in east2; response quality might differ. Notify product and CS.

customer-success-olivia: Notifying affected customers: telling them we are diverting low-priority traffic and working on a capacity fix. We'll offer targeted retries in 30m.

sre-maya: running command to adjust routing policy:
```bash
# update routing policy to prefer east2 for low-priority routes
redwoodctl routes update --route inference.low-priority --prefer-region us-east-2 --force-evacuate
```

incidents-bot: automated check: route update applied, 78% of low-priority traffic now directed to us-east-2. Queue in us-west-3 growth rate slowed.

palmer: telemetry: queued requests in us-west-3 dropped from 4.1k -> 1.8k in 3m after steer started. However, acme-prod remains >60% affected (they're pinned to prod high-priority endpoint).

oncall-anna: next for acme-prod: enable circuit-breaker to shed non-critical tokens and apply per-customer emergency quota. Can ops apply an emergency per-customer rate-limit to acme-prod to prevent full-queue takeover?

infra-ops: yes. applying per-customer QPS cap of 20 on their route. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl quotas set --customer acme-inc --route generation --qps 20 --reason "emergency us-west-3 capacity"
```

incidents-bot: quota change accepted. acme-inc QPS dropped, their tail latency improved slightly. Overall error rate for acme down from 42% -> 18% after cap + reroutes.

eng-runtime-lead: note: autoscaler still failing on quotaExceeded. We should patch autoscaler to degrade more gracefully: when provision fails, it can try multi-region provision logic (fall back to east2) rather than retrying same region. Filing quick PR now.

sre-maya: rolling temporary config to add region-fallback to autoscaler (hotfix). Patch id: PR#1427. Deploying to canary autoscaler.

palmer: customer impact summary for ops: acme-prod had ~2.5k requests affected over 18m window, peak 52% error rate. Beta-saas and internal tests impacted lower magnitude. No data loss, only latency/timeouts.

customer-success-olivia: customers informed, ACME rep acknowledged and accepted rate-limited mitigation but requested ETA for full recovery.

infra-ops: cloud quota ticket updated, asked for emergency quota expansion. Meanwhile, we can spin up 6 GPUs from dedicated-reserve to us-west-3 manually (requires ops approval). That would reduce queue by ~1.2k. Ops: proceed?

oncall-anna: go ahead with reserve allocation + continue steering. Prioritize automation fix after immediate stabilization.

infra-ops: allocating reserve pool now. Logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:28:10Z reserve.ctrl: allocating 6 gpus -> success
2026-03-15T10:28:12Z pool-manager: pool size increased by 6 gpus, capacity available
```

incidents-bot: Post-action checks: us-west-3 queued requests down to 600, overall 95th latency back to ~1.6s for SLA routes. Best-effort still slightly degraded.

palmer: ops checklist: 1) confirm autoscaler hotfix merged+deployed, 2) confirm cloud quota escalation response, 3) scale down reserved allocation once autoscaler healthy, 4) RCA to follow. Assigning owners: eng-runtime-lead (autoscaler fix), infra-ops (quota ticket + reserve), customer-success-olivia (customer comms).

eng-runtime-lead: hotfix merged to main, canary shows successful multi-region provision attempts when local quota hit. Rolling to prod in 5m.

sre-maya: monitoring metrics show no regression during canary. Proceeding with staged rollout.

customer-success-olivia: ACME wants post-incident notes and whether we can avoid future pinning. I'll coordinate a postmortem action item.

oncall-anna: summary so far: cause = regional GPU quota exhaustion in us-west-3 + autoscaler lacking multi-region fallback. Mitigations = reroute low-priority traffic, per-customer emergency QPS caps, allocate reserved GPUs, patch autoscaler. Current status = stabilized, some best-effort requests still degraded.

palmer: creating incident channel and postmortem doc. Will include timeline and metric graphs.

incidents-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. escalation -> monitor for 2 hours. Please update handoff if leaving on-call. :white_check_mark:

oncall-anna: handing off to @sre-maya for monitoring window. Leaving now.

sre-maya: acknowledged, I'll monitor for 2h and escalate if queue starts to climb again.

support-jordan: will follow up with customers as needed.

customer-success-olivia: scheduling post-incident review with ACME for tomorrow at 11am PT.

palmer: ETA for full recovery depends on cloud quota increase; if granted, we'll scale down reserves. Otherwise we'll keep the reserve and consider capacity reservations for big customers.

incidents-bot: event closed for now. Logs and timeline stored at https://redwood.internal/incidents/1875001234 for the postmortem.
